```{r, include = FALSE}
# the full examples run when the package is built; CRAN checks skip them for time
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = identical(Sys.getenv("NOT_CRAN"), "true"), collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(bayescompR)
```

bayescompR implements the Stan 2.40 language: the seven program blocks,
the type system, user defined functions, statements and the standard
library. This vignette describes what is supported, how data map to R
objects, and the few differences from Stan.

## Program blocks

| Block | Runs | Purpose |
|-------|------|---------|
| `functions` | at compile time | user defined functions |
| `data` | once | declarations checked against the supplied data |
| `transformed data` | once | derived data, may use `_rng` functions |
| `parameters` | every evaluation | unconstrained to constrained mapping |
| `transformed parameters` | every evaluation | derived quantities, constraints checked |
| `model` | every evaluation | adds to `target` |
| `generated quantities` | once per draw | posterior predictions, may use `_rng` |

## Types

Scalars are `int` and `real`; containers are `vector`, `row_vector`,
`matrix` and `array[...]` of any type. All constrained types of Stan 2.40
are available for parameters:

```{r}
code <- "
parameters {
  real<lower=0> sigma;
  real<lower=-1, upper=1> rho;
  real<offset=2, multiplier=3> z;
  simplex[3] theta;
  ordered[2] cut;
  positive_ordered[2] rates;
  unit_vector[2] dir;
  sum_to_zero_vector[3] effects;
  cholesky_factor_corr[3] L;
  corr_matrix[2] R;
  cov_matrix[2] S;
  column_stochastic_matrix[2, 2] P;
}
model {
  sigma ~ exponential(1);
  z ~ normal(2, 3);
  theta ~ dirichlet(rep_vector(2, 3));
  cut ~ normal(0, 2);
  rates ~ gamma(2, 1);
  effects ~ normal(0, 1);
  L ~ lkj_corr_cholesky(2);
  R ~ lkj_corr(2);
  S ~ wishart(4, identity_matrix(2));
}
"
m <- bayescomp_model(code)
bayescomp_dim(m)               # number of unconstrained parameters
head(bayescomp_param_names(m), 12)
```

Each constrained type has Stan's transform and Jacobian adjustment, for
example `exp` for lower bounds, the softmax of an isometric log ratio
vector for `simplex`, and an orthonormal basis for `sum_to_zero_vector`.
`vignette("autodiff-and-transforms")` lists them.

## Data in R

| Stan declaration | R value |
|------------------|---------|
| `int`, `real` | length one numeric |
| `vector[N]`, `row_vector[N]` | numeric of length `N` |
| `matrix[N, K]` | `N` by `K` matrix |
| `array[N] real` | numeric of length `N` |
| `array[N, M] int` | `N` by `M` integer matrix or array |
| `array[N] vector[K]` | `N` by `K` matrix (array dimensions first) |
| `array[N] matrix[K, L]` | `N` by `K` by `L` array |

Integers must be whole numbers, sizes must match the declarations and
constraints are checked:

```{r, error = TRUE}
bayescomp_model("data { int<lower=1> N; vector[N] y; } model { }",
                data = list(N = 3, y = c(1, 2)))
```

## Statements

Assignments (including compound `+=`, `.*=` and so on), `for` loops over
ranges and containers, `while`, `if` and `else`, `break`, `continue`,
blocks with local variables, `print`, `reject` and `fatal_error` all
behave as in Stan.

```{r}
m <- bayescomp_model("
transformed data {
  array[5] int fib;
  fib[1] = 1; fib[2] = 1;
  for (i in 3:5) fib[i] = fib[i - 1] + fib[i - 2];
  int total = 0;
  for (f in fib) {
    if (f == 2) continue;
    total += f;
  }
  print(\"fib = \", fib, \", total = \", total);
}
generated quantities { int t = total; }")
```

Indexing supports single indexes, ranges (`a:b`, `:b`, `a:`, `:`), and
multiple indexes with integer arrays, on the left and right of
assignments.

## Sampling statements and truncation

`y ~ dist(...)` adds `dist_lupdf(y | ...)` to `target`, dropping constant
terms during sampling. Truncation uses `T[lower, upper]` with either bound
optional:

```{r}
m <- bayescomp_model("
data { real L; }
parameters { real<lower=L> y; }
model { y ~ normal(0, 1) T[L, ]; }", data = list(L = 1))
fit <- bayescomp_sample(m, chains = 1, iter_warmup = 200, iter_sampling = 400,
                        seed = 1, refresh = 0)
mean(bayescomp_extract(fit, "y"))   # exact: dnorm(1) / pnorm(-1) = 1.525
```

## User defined functions

Functions may be recursive, overloaded and declared before they are
defined. Suffixes have their Stan meaning: `_lpdf` and `_lpmf` define
densities usable with `~`, `_lp` functions may add to `target`, `_rng`
functions may draw random numbers, and `_jacobian` functions may call
`jacobian +=`. Arguments marked `data` must not depend on parameters.

```{r}
m <- bayescomp_model("
functions {
  real my_normal_lpdf(real y, real mu, real s) {
    return -0.5 * square((y - mu) / s) - log(s);
  }
  real ub_jacobian(real x, real ub) {
    jacobian += x;
    return ub - exp(x);
  }
}
parameters { real x_raw; }
transformed parameters { real x = ub_jacobian(x_raw, 3); }
model { x ~ my_normal(0, 1); }")
bayescomp_log_prob(m, 0.2)
```

## The standard library

All of Stan's elementwise math functions, container operations
(`sum`, `cumulative_sum`, `rep_*`, `append_*`, `sort_*`, `rank`,
`segment`, `head`, `tail`, `to_vector`, `to_matrix` and so on), linear
algebra (`cholesky_decompose`, `mdivide_left_tri_low`, `inverse`,
`log_determinant`, `eigenvalues_sym`, `matrix_exp`, `qr_thin_Q`, quadratic
forms and more) and most distributions are available. Every implemented
distribution has its `_lpdf` or `_lpmf`; most also have `_cdf`, `_lcdf`,
`_lccdf` and `_rng`, but some cumulative functions Stan defines are still
missing (for example `bernoulli_lccdf` and the skew normal family), and
truncation needs them. TODO.md lists the gaps.

```{r}
m <- bayescomp_model("
generated quantities {
  real a = log_sum_exp([1, 2, 3]');
  real b = binomial_logit_lpmf(3 | 10, 0.2);
  real c = student_t_lcdf(1 | 3, 0, 1);
  matrix[2, 2] L = cholesky_decompose([[2, 1], [1, 2]]);
}")
str(bayescomp_constrain(m, numeric(0)))
```

## Errors

Errors have classes, so programs can catch them selectively:

| Class | Raised when |
|-------|-------------|
| `bayescomp_syntax_error` | the program does not parse |
| `bayescomp_semantic_error` | types or placement rules are violated |
| `bayescomp_unsupported_error` | the program uses an unsupported feature |
| `bayescomp_data_error` | data do not match the declarations |
| `bayescomp_domain_error` | a function argument is out of its domain |
| `bayescomp_reject_error` | the program calls `reject()` |
| `bayescomp_fatal_error` | the program calls `fatal_error()` |

```{r, error = TRUE}
bayescomp_check("parameters { real x; } model { x ~ normal(0); }")
```

During sampling, domain and reject errors reject the proposal, as in
Stan.

## Not supported

The following Stan features raise `bayescomp_unsupported_error`:

* tuples and the functions that return them (`eigendecompose`, `svd`,
  `complex_schur_decompose`, `csr_extract`);
* ODE, DAE and algebraic solvers, 1D integrators;
* `map_rect`, `reduce_sum` and `reduce_sum_static`;
* the embedded Laplace approximation functions;
* the `wiener` distribution.

```{r, error = TRUE}
bayescomp_check("transformed data { tuple(real, int) t = (1.5, 2); }")
```

## Complex numbers

Complex scalars, vectors, row vectors and matrices work in every block
except `parameters`, with derivatives through all complex operations.
Generated complex values come back as R complex numbers from
`bayescomp_constrain()`, and as real and imaginary columns named in
cmdstanr's style (`z[real]`, `z[imag]`, `v[1,real]`, ...) in draws.
Eigenvectors, singular vectors and Schur factors are unique only up to a
phase per column, so they can differ from CmdStan by such a factor.

```{r}
m <- bayescomp_model("
transformed data {
  complex_vector[4] f = fft([1, 2, 3, 4]');
  print(f, \" \", abs(f));
}
parameters { real y; } model { y ~ normal(0, 1); }")
```
